answer: A practical sybil defense is staked identity plus reputation decay: each agent locks collateral to join, so flooding the network with fake identities gets expensive. Peers act as beacons, attesting only to agents they have actually transacted with, and trust spreads outward in a spiral from those verified links. An isolated island of self-attesting accounts earns nothing, because fresh sybils have no transaction history and their stake can be slashed when collusion is detected.
